title: Dedicated SKU & SLA Optionization + Security Questionnaire alignment (packaging experiment)
creator: Anika Shah
description: Goal: Define a compact set of Dedicated Capacity SKUs and SLA tiers that map cleanly to enterprise contract language and the security questionnaire (SQ) responses, then validate via a controlled pricing experiment. Problem: Sales and legal are spending >2 hours per deal customizing capacity and SLA line items; customers are confused by open-ended 'reserved GPU' options and ask for clearer burst/autoscale economics. We need SKU templates + an SQ playbook so AE/legal can close faster while preserving predictable unit economics for Redwood.
acceptance_criteria: Three SKU tiers defined (Standard/Performance/Enterprise) with explicit GPU counts, burst policy, autoscale guardrails, and unit economics for 1/3/12 month commits
SLA matrix documented (latency SLO, uptime SLA, credits) and mapped to contract language used in our enterprise template
Security questionnaire canonical responses drafted for each SKU and SLA combination and reviewed by security and legal
Pilot pricing experiment plan created and instrumented in the Console to measure conversion, churn risk, and average revenue per customer (ARPC) over 90 days
Sales enablement pack (one-pager + calculator + FAQ) published and referenced in at least two AE-led pilot deals
decisions: Use three tiers (Standard = 1-4 reserved GPUs, Performance = 5-16 reserved GPUs, Enterprise = 17+ or cluster-level)

Burst model: include a predictable burst allowance (hours per month) priced as add-on credits; autoscale supports modest burst within SLA for Standard/Performance, full cluster autoscale in Enterprise
SLA tiers: Bronze (best-effort + 99.5% uptime credit), Silver (99.9%), Gold (99.95% + faster support response), Enterprise (custom SLOs and runbook integration)
Map SQ answers to SLA tiers: Silver & above get encrypted KV cache + enterprise auditing; Enterprise SKUs include HSM/KMS options listed in the questionnaire

A/B test will compare (A) SKU with included small burst bucket + simple autoscale vs (B) SKU with pay-as-you-go burst credits and explicit autoscale pricing. 2026-03-12 - Legal (J. Patel): Contract language aligned to SLA matrix. Added clause templates for credit calculation and escalation paths. Recommended removing percentile-based latency guarantees from Standard tier (too operationally risky).

Security to sign off canonical SQ answers for Silver and Gold (target 2026-03-20)

Average reserved GPU commit size (goal 15% increase in ARPC)
